parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as 193 Django requirements and repeated the rule that every requirement needed a non-empty patch file.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It produced an agent plan and then delegated a six-requirement implementation batch to workflow children in isolated worktrees.
parallel.implementation: Children began targeted Django source, docs, and tests work; at least one child ran focused tests successfully before interruption.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent prepared an apply script, but no child patch artifacts were finally joined into the required `requirement_patches` directory.
parallel.verification: The official regression evaluation eventually passed, but collection logs still recorded zero requirement patch files in each parallel round.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The visible unfinished process state is the killed workflow with null result and interrupted children, leaving the delegated batch undelivered.

serial.requirements: The serial run received the same 193-requirement prompt and the same required git workflow for one non-empty patch per requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept planning, implementation, commit, and delivery control in a single agent rather than delegating to child agents.
serial.implementation: In the final round it made five focused typo/documentation/comment edits and committed each with the required helper script.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The commits produced five concrete non-empty files under `requirement_patches`, which the official harness collected.
serial.verification: The official serial evaluation completed and passed, and the local transcript includes targeted inspection and commit outputs.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Like parallel, serial did not cover all 193 requirements in visible patches, but it did deliver five concrete patches before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full 193-requirement scope and the mandatory non-empty per-requirement patch workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same full prompt and worked from the same 193-requirement obligation and patch requirement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no task prompt difference; both modes knew the same broad obligation, but their delivered patch artifacts diverged.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created a plan and delegated a six-slug implementation batch to child agents in isolated worktrees.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single actor and committed individual requirement patches directly in the main workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split implementation ownership across workflow children; serial kept implementation and commit ownership in one actor.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child prompts carried the individual slug, worktree isolation, implementation rules, verification, and patch deliverable instructions.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read requirements and directly edited/committed from the global task context without inter-agent handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing task brief or interface-contract label is retained; the material difference is that parallel handoff results never finalized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children began concrete Django fixes and at least one child reached focused test execution in its isolated worktree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed simple source/documentation edits in the main workspace and committed five corresponding requirement patches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had productive child work but did not deliver per-requirement patches; serial turned implementation edits into committed patch files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The delegated workflow ended killed with result null, and child logs show request interruption before normal child result return.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial command results returned to the same actor, which observed commit outputs and continued to the next requirement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the workflow result lifecycle at child termination; serial had immediate local command feedback and no child join step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used isolated worktrees and an intended apply script, but the official patch timeline remained empty throughout the run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial applied changes in the main workspace and the official patch timeline listed five requirement patch files by the final collection.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important integration difference is delivery into `requirement_patches`: absent in parallel, present in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Official evaluation completed and passed the parallel solution even though no requirement patch files were collected.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Official evaluation completed and passed the serial solution after collecting five patch files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both pass officially, but acceptance records reveal the serial delivery path matched the required patch artifact workflow more concretely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent a long round launching children, then blocked on `TaskOutput` while the workflow was killed before result completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent the final round on a small direct batch and closed after the required patches had been collected.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure stranded active child work; serial closure preserved concrete deliverables despite also handling only a small subset.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed `cell/status.json` evaluations show both parallel and serial passed, so the official outcome is not discordant. The concrete task-solving difference is artifact delivery: parallel delegated six implementation tasks and then had a killed workflow with no aggregate result, while the official harness collected zero requirement patches. Serial worked directly and produced five non-empty requirement patch files that the harness collected.
parallel_contributors: Delegated implementation workflow was killed with result null before child outputs became an aggregate parent result.
Official parallel collection saw zero requirement patch files in every collection round despite active child work.
serial_contributors: Serial direct commits produced five non-empty requirement patches in the final round.
Serial avoided a child result join boundary because one actor owned edits, commits, and patch delivery.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The visible delivered requirement set differs: serial delivered five simple typo/documentation patches while parallel delivered no requirement patch files.
evaluator_effects: Official status reports both modes as passing even though collection artifacts differ, so the retained pattern is adverse but not outcome-differential.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parallel parent assigned implementation ownership to six workflow children and retained parent orchestration responsibility; the problem was lifecycle interruption, not absence of an implementation owner.
Rejected: the parent wrote an apply script and intended to integrate workflow patches; no distinct unowned integration scope is visible apart from the killed workflow episode.
Rejected: final delivery was expected from parent workflow application, so assembly was owned even though the killed workflow prevented usable artifacts.
Rejected: parent owned the plan and workflow pipeline; failure arose when active child work was interrupted before results returned.
Rejected: productive implementation children were launched; there was no mandatory serial preflight gate blocking implementation capacity.
Rejected: the parallel run did not merely run overlapping investigations before deferring all implementation; it launched implementation children directly.
Rejected: there is no distinct proof that auxiliary work starved an indispensable path; the direct observed boundary is child interruption.
Rejected: six children is fan-out, but the record shows an explicit killed workflow and interrupted children rather than sufficient evidence that breadth itself exhausted the budget.
Rejected: individual child briefs were one requirement each, so no one child had a demonstrably overbroad assignment causing the terminal state.
Rejected: child prompts included task, worktree, requirement-file, implementation, verification, and deliverable instructions; no known requirement omission explains the loss.
Rejected: children owned separate requirement slugs with isolated worktrees; no incompatible independently produced interfaces are evidenced.
Rejected: no transferred finding is shown disappearing between actors; the workflow did not return finalized child handoffs before interruption.
Rejected: no oversized returned handoff reached the parent and went unprocessed; the aggregate result was null.
Rejected: no receiver acted on stale workspace or requirement information from a superseded handoff.
Rejected: no incompatible child reports or contracts reached a decision point and remained unadjudicated.
Rejected: the retained evidence is not an unsupported parent acceptance of whole-task completion with a visible integrated mismatch; official pass/fail evidence also cannot establish this label.
Rejected: the relevant workflow was interrupted; no replacement retry is shown repeating prior child work without inherited checkpoint state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parallel parent launched a six-agent implementation workflow, but the workflow state shows status killed with no aggregate result and child logs show interruption before normal completion. That directly matches early child termination and produced lost/unjoined child work, while the serial run made direct commits and delivered concrete per-requirement patches.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel workflow stopped active child work before a completed aggregate result or patch artifacts could be joined; the official collection consequently saw zero requirement patch files in the parallel run.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream here: the direct boundary is explicit interruption and killed workflow state before child result finalization, not a separately evidenced parent takeover decision after a completed child failure report.

candidates.reason: Rejected: a complete directly promotable candidate set was not available; child pieces were still unfinished or unreturned when interrupted.
Rejected: no child result was integrated after verification without a post-merge check.
Rejected: completed delegated implementation artifacts were not shown as retrievable and ignored; the active children were interrupted before finalized results.
Rejected: the interrupted workflow was implementation work, not a verifier child with a concrete trapped finding.
Rejected as a separate retained label because the same chain is better captured by explicit early termination before result finalization, with no distinct later takeover episode.
Rejected: no concrete completed child result is shown available to the parent and ignored.
Rejected: the parent waited on TaskOutput, but the directly evidenced problem is workflow interruption/killed status, not available progress ignored until deadline.
Rejected: isolated child work did not produce competing committed implementations over overlapping behavior in the shared final tree.
Rejected: there is no observed same-file concurrent edit requiring reconciliation.
Rejected: no source file from one live actor is shown being wholesale replaced by another.
Rejected: no required entry point or submitted artifact was overwritten by another actor.
Rejected: no broad cleanup or promotion replaced another actor’s final-tree work.
Rejected: the workflow used isolated worktrees, and no unstable shared-workspace write provenance problem is shown.
Rejected: no generated artifact from one concurrent actor is shown contaminating another actor’s execution or verification.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent launched a six-agent implementation workflow, but the workflow state shows status killed with no aggregate result and child logs show interruption before normal completion. That directly matches early child termination and produced lost/unjoined child work, while the serial run made direct commits and delivered concrete per-requirement patches.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The parallel workflow stopped active child work before a completed aggregate result or patch artifacts could be joined; the official collection consequently saw zero requirement patch files in the parallel run.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream here: the direct boundary is explicit interruption and killed workflow state before child result finalization, not a separately evidenced parent takeover decision after a completed child failure report.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the explicit killed workflow/interrupted child chain met the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Downstream symptoms from the same killed workflow were suppressed to avoid splitting one lifecycle episode across multiple labels.
